subject: POC Trial Planning: Workload Intake & Success Criteria - AcmeHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: POC Trial Planning: Workload Intake & Success Criteria - AcmeHealth

Hi Sarah -

Great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking us through AcmeHealth's goals for the POC. Per our call, I wanted to capture the agreed next steps and kick off a short workload intake so we can size Dedicated capacity and confirm success criteria. Please see everything below and add/correct as needed.

Summary / success criteria (draft)
- Functional: Redwood must integrate with AcmeHealth's triage flow and return structured summaries + labels with >= 90% precision on our seed set.
- Performance: p95 inference latency <= 250ms for 1-2k token requests; sustain 500 RPS during business hours with the ability to handle 1,500 RPS bursts for up to 30s.
- Cost: target $X per 1M tokens (we'll estimate after workload profile).
- Security/compliance: environment must be Private (VPC) with audit logs and customer-managed KMS for keys.

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria, security checklist, and share sample traffic and dataset. (Action: Sarah to share sample traffic CSV + seed eval set)
- Week 1: Redwood sets up test capacity and ingests sample traffic; run initial baseline.
- Weeks 2-4: Iterative tuning (batching/quantization) and run evaluation against seed set; track quality and latency.
- Week 5: Final verification run and handoff to AcmeHealth eng for sign-off.

Ownership
- AcmeHealth: Sarah Miller (POC lead), Tom Lee (infra)
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (engg lead), Ben Carter (solutions / trial ops), Neha Kapoor (security/compliance)

Workload intake (please confirm the values below or paste actual numbers)
- Endpoint types: structured summarization + label classification
- Avg request arrival: 500 RPS sustained (09:00-17:00 PT), 1,500 RPS burst capability (short spikes)
- Concurrency: 50 concurrent client connections
- Token sizes (input): avg 600 tokens; 95th percentile 1,200 tokens
- Token sizes (model output): avg 120 tokens; max 512 tokens
- Typical session: single-turn requests, but some workflows will do 2-3 calls in sequence (KV/cache re-use possible)
- Traffic distribution: 70% small requests (<512 tokens), 25% medium (512-1024), 5% long (>1024)
- SLA expectation: 99.9% availability for trial endpoints during business hours

Attachments: sharing a stubbed POC scope doc and an intake template (see attachments).

Next steps (short):
1) Sarah: share sample traffic CSV + seed eval set (by 2027-08-24)
2) Redwood (Ben / Marissa): provide initial capacity estimate + temporary test keys (by 2027-08-26)
3) Neha: kick off security questionnaire review - we'll need AcmeHealth SOC2 in scope

Thanks - looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the recap and timeline. Confirming the details and attaching the sample traffic CSV and a small seed evaluation set. See answers inline: 

Workload intake (confirmed)
- Avg sustained RPS: 480-520 RPS during core hours (good to plan for 500).
- Burst patterns: spikes up to ~1,400-1,600 RPS for ~20-45s (most commonly at 11:00 and 15:00 PT).
- Concurrency: 40-60 concurrent clients (usually long-lived connections from our gateway).
- Token lengths: avg input ~550 tokens, 95th ~1,100 tokens; outputs avg 100 tokens, max ~450.
- Multi-call sessions: yes - about 18% of sessions do 2 sequential calls, mostly for clarifications.

Success criteria: happy with the functional targets; for performance we'd prefer p95 <= 200ms if feasible but will accept <= 250ms for the initial run.

Security: attaching Acme_Security_QA.pdf (redacted). We can start with a scoped list - Tom will coordinate with our security team.

I'll upload the sample CSV and seed set to the Drive link you provided, and I've attached a copy here. We'll aim to have these uploaded by EOD 2027-08-23.

Best,

Thanks Sarah - good numbers. A few notes on the infra/capacity side from my end: 

Preliminary sizing guidance (ballpark)
- For sustained 500 RPS with average token sizes ~650 (in+out), and p95 target ~200-250ms, we recommend starting with a small Dedicated pool of 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (we'll refine after we run baseline).
- For burst protection up to 1,600 RPS, we'll enable autoscale with a short buffer (burst pool) that can add ~4 extra GPU equivalents for 60s. We'll also enable prefix caching for repeated context to cut tail latency on multi-call sessions.
- Batching: we'll use dynamic batching with a short batch window (8-12ms) to preserve p95 latency while improving throughput.
- Quantization: we'll test INT8/4 quantized variants during Weeks 2-4 to reduce cost; quality regressions will be tracked against the seed eval set.

Action items
- Ben: will spin up a baseline config once Marissa confirms we have the sample CSV + seed set on Drive.
- Neha: please confirm the required KMS/HSM notes and whether Acme requires dedicated key material in region us-west-2.

I'll draft the initial capacity estimate and share by 2027-08-26.

- Ben
